text:
Connor Bedard is hurt again, and the Blackhawks have spent the last week proving there is life without him. They have won three straight, outscoring teams 13-7, behind a run from their young players that nobody would have scripted.

Sam Rinzel has 15 points in his last 10 games against six our numbers expected, enough to earn the NHL's third star honors. Roman Kantserov, who scored plenty in the KHL, scored his first career hat trick in a 6-3 win over the Canucks and has 12 points in 10. Frank Nazar has 11, and his line with Patrick Kane and Oliver Moore gets 57% of the expected goals, the best of the regulars.

Here is the honest part. Rinzel is running at more than twice his expected pace, and the winning streak was half earned: Chicago got 52% of the chances in those games, with the goaltending stopping three more goals than expected. Over the season the Hawks get 44% of the expected goals at 5v5 and have allowed 96 goals in 25 games. Arvid Soderblom is at .846 over his last four starts. The Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov pair has been outscored 15-4, and Kaiser is now serving a three-game suspension for his hit on Calgary's Martin Pospisil.

At 9-14-2, our simulations give Chicago a 1% playoff chance. That makes this a development year, and the development is the story. What to watch: how much of Rinzel's run survives the regression.
headline: Rinzel and Kantserov light up a lost season
